thread:
maya: heads up — customers are seeing model=redwood-small returned even when header X-Model-Override=redwood-medium is present. failing traffic shows 200 OK but wrong model route. :thinking:
kevin: ugh. route matching or header precedence bug. any decision logs for those requests?
lena: we only sample 0.05% of routing traces currently, so most requests won't have traces. did you check the sampling flag for that tenant?
maya: i looked. tenant=acme-corp shows sample_rate: 0.0005 in /internal/config/route-sampling. but i can repro locally with curl to our gateway and enable debug header.
kevin: what debug header? we have X-Redwood-Debug:trace but it's supposed to be gated by config. send exact curl you used.
maya: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Model-Override: redwood-medium" -H "X-Redwood-Debug: trace" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
kevin: nice — does /internal/routing/eval return anything for that request id? you can call: curl "http://router-internal:8080/debug/eval?request_id=<id>"
maya: tracebot posted a short decision id: dec-9f3a8b. i did curl http://router-internal:8080/debug/eval?decision_id=dec-9f3a8b and got a 204.
lena: 204 means we didn't persist that trace because sampling kicked it out. tracebot should still have a stub event though. can you paste the gateway logs around the request? just the 2-3 lines with route evaluation.
maya: pasted: ```
[router] 2025-10-03T14:03:21Z INFO eval_start request=req/0x9a1
[router] 2025-10-03T14:03:21Z DEBUG headers {"X-Model-Override": "redwood-medium", "tenant": "acme-corp"}
[router] 2025-10-03T14:03:21Z INFO selected_rule rule=default-model-route variant=redwood-small reason="header_not_matched"
```
kevin: aha — header shows up but rule says header_not_matched. maybe header matching is case-sensitive or we changed header canonicalization recently. which rule config exists for model override? sahil: i can pull it. rule looks like: match: headers.X-Model-Override == "redwood-medium" -> variant redwood-medium. it's using exact match.
sahil: also noticed we recently added header canonicalization to lowercase keys at proxy level. but our rule engine expects original-case header names (X-Model-Override). mismatch there.
lena: good catch. we should either canonicalize rule keys when loading or normalize header names at evaluation time. quick mitigation: add alias header "x-model-override" to the rule config. maya can you hotpatch the rule for acme-corp to include both forms?
maya: i'll add rule alias and then run small check. patch command: ```
POST /internal/rules/acme-corp/_patch
{ "add": [{"match": "headers.x-model-override == \"redwood-medium\"", "variant": "redwood-medium"}]}
```
ingress-bot: deploy triggered for rules-acme-corp v2025-10-03_1406 :rocket:
kevin: while that's rolling, let's also expose a forced-trace header for debugging so sampling doesn't drop it. we already have X-Redwood-Debug:trace but it's RBAC gated. proposal: allow X-Redwood-Trace:1 for requests from internal subnets or with support token to force persist. create small RFC?
lena: agreed. i'll add a tiny console toggle under Debug -> Routing traces to flip sampling to 100% for given tenant or path for 10m. UX should warn about cost.
sahil: for long-term fix i'll open infra task to normalize header names in the rule compiler. quick note: need to update rule schema docs too.
maya: after patch, i retried. logs now: ```
[router] INFO selected_rule rule=default-model-route variant=redwood-medium reason="header_matched:alias"
[router] INFO decision_persisted id=dec-9f3a8b sampler=forced
```
maya: and tracebot now returns full decision trace at /debug/eval?decision_id=dec-9f3a8b
kevin: great. next steps: 1) short RFC for forced-trace header and console toggle (lena) 2) normalize header keys in compiler + tests (sahil) 3) add metric routing.trace.sampled_count and alert if forced traces spike (ops)
lena: i'll draft the RFC tonight and add to eng-platform backlog. tagging @sahil for the compiler task. :thumbsup:
kevin: one more ask — can we include the matched_expression and evaluated_headers in the decision log for root cause, so the UI can show why a header was considered matched vs not? small change to trace schema but super useful.
sahil: sounds fine. will add fields matched_expr (string) and headers_snapshot (map) to persisted trace. note: logs schema change needs migration across trace consumers.
maya: thanks everyone. will monitor acme-corp for the next hour and post if anything else pops up. :eyes:
